swing_ideas.text: Inverted head and shoulders. If the broad market can hold up, looking for a move to break the neckline over 151.15. Any higher lows above, are then great Brigade Bolt™ setups for continuation to 166.5 area.

Bull flag consolidation post earnings. Over the highs are also a cup and handle breakout, and a double bottom breakout. Over 11.55 and theres pretty thin structure into the 13.67 area, beyond that its 15.37. Theoretically RSI could cool off here before the break.

Daily bull flag, weekly three bar play. Huge rounded base on the higher timeframe. Overhead supply lows should be the target above. Not interested if the 10 level breaks, would require a deeper pullback to 6.5 for the gap close.

sections: S&P daily chart – We're going to look back at the Fitch downgrade as an example of how trends change. The market fell ~10% from Aug-Nov 2023.

S&P weekly chart – The main idea in that timeframe was that the weekly pullback was going to offer a monthly higher low over the inverted head and shoulders reversal from the 2022 drawdown. That ended up marking the low.

S&P weekly chart – So where does the weekly trend sit? Well we just broke for a higher high over the prior pivot at 577. There is plenty of opportunity for a higher low over 577, 570 gap close, or 550 as the curve ball.

S&P daily chart – If you want this to play out like Fitch, you want to see this path below. Overshoot the gap close at 570, set a weekly lower high, double top over 570 with a break back below that level being the time and place to get short on a completed reversal. 570 is your huckleberry.
S&P daily chart – What seems more reasonable to me, is some kind of hold over the top of the gap, or a gap fill reversal off of 567.75 that seeks a higher low back over 577.
S&P hourly chart – pathing ideas and locations where R:R may favor some kind of trade developing. (F.O. = Forecast Open)

Market internals – On Thursday, sellers had a shot at rolling the market over via an open under Wednesday's value... No dice. Internals closed neutral to bullish. Moral of the story? Stronger sellers still aren't involved. We'll see if early in the week that changes with the Moody's news.
Market profile – Value is clearly higher, and the nuance to take away is again, weakness from sellers on Thursday, unable to break through the Wednesday low and rotate through the single prints.
